reason: Quote and mechanism are exact: ArenaManager.java:578 is verbatim 'spawns.add(readLocationFromMap(map, worldName, id + ".spawn-points." + index));', readLocationFromMap (640-651) has no local try/catch, and mapDouble (653-659) throws IllegalArgumentException on a missing or non-finite x/y/z, while the sibling readOptionalLocation (687-695) demonstrates the guard that spawn points deliberately do not get. The exception therefore escapes readDefinition and is caught only by load()'s per-arena catch (188-191), so registry.register at line 186 is never reached and the whole definition disappears; ArenaResetService.resolve (541-543) then returns null and canReset returns ARENA_NOT_FOUND (187), exactly as claimed. Reachability survives the validator test: YamlFiles.arenasValidator (163-239) inspects only schema-version, presence of the arenas section, thin/empty-arena truncation shape and a non-blank 'world' - it never inspects spawn-point coordinates - so a hand-edited entry such as 'y:' with no value, or 'x: .NaN', passes the sentinel and reaches readDefinition, and the same holds for mob-spawn-points at line 592. Severity is nevertheless overstated at medium: every plugin-side writer emits all three coordinates from Location getters (AdminDeployManager.saveSpawnPoints 481-500, ArenaAdminService.copyEntry/deleteYamlEntry 682-732), file writes are whole-file atomic via unique temp name + ATOMIC_MOVE (YamlFiles.write 111-125), so only a manual edit or external corruption can produce the malformed map, and no arena data is lost - the on-disk definition, including every valid spawn point, is intact and the fix is a one-line YAML correction plus restart. The failure is also loud rather than silent: load() logs 'Skipping damaged arena definition: <arenaId>' with the full stack trace naming the exact path (e.g. 'Missing or invalid y at arena1.spawn-points.0'), so the admin is not left without a diagnostic. This is a real robustness gap that contradicts the codebase's own stated invariant (ArenaManager.java:556-557 and 681-683 both justify tolerating damaged core/shop-npc precisely because a throw would erase the arena from the registry), but its practical impact is a hand-edit misconfiguration with a clear console error, not a medium-severity defect.
